bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

0 total 8 drwxr-xr-x. 1 agent agent 62 Jun 11 22:25 . drwxr-xr-x. 1 agent agent 18 Jun 11 22:25 .. -rw-r--r--. 1 agent agent 1228 Jun 11 22:25 dstask-import.md -rw-r--r--. 1 agent agent 970 Jun 11 22:25 taskwarrior-migration.md

dstask

Single binary terminal-based TODO manager with git-based sync + markdown notes per task




Dstask is a personal task tracker designed to help you focus. It is similar to [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) but uses git to synchronise instead of a special protocol. If you're at home in the terminal, and with solving the occasional merge conflict, then dstask is for you! https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589d06fd-7486-46e4-b838-ce85af12f0fc [Video courtesy of xGoivo -- thanks!](https://www.reddit.com/r/taskwarrior/comments/1o7itzg/what_do_you_guys_think_about_this_taskwarrior/) ## Features - Powerful context system (automatically applies filter/tags to queries and new tasks) - **Git powered sync**/undo/resolve ([passwordstore.org](https://www.passwordstore.org/) style) which means no need to set up a sync server, and syncing between devices is easy! - Task listing won't break with long task text - `note` command -- edit a **full markdown note** for each task. **Checklists are useful here.** - `open` command -- **open URLs found in specified task** (including notes) in the browser - zsh/bash completion (including tags and projects in current context) for speed; PowerShell completion on Windows - A single statically-linked binary - import tool which can import GitHub issues or taskwarrior tasks. ## Non-features - Collaboration. This is a personal task tracker. Use another system for projects that involve multiple people. Note that it can still be beneficial to use dstask to track what you are working on in the context of a multi-person project tracked elsewhere. ## Requirements - Git - A 256-color capable terminal ## Installation 1. Copy the executable (from the [releases page][releases]) to somewhere in your PATH. - Linux/macOS: name it `dstask` and mark it executable (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/`). - Windows: use `dstask.exe` and place it in a directory on `PATH` (e.g. `%USERPROFILE%\bin`). 1. Enable shell completions: - Bash: add `source <(dstask bash-completion)` to your `.bashrc`. - Zsh: add `dstask zsh-completion > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_dstask` or source completions in your `~/.zshrc`. - PowerShell (Windows): see section "PowerShell completion" below. 1. Set up an alias in your `.bashrc`: `alias task=dstask` or `alias t=dstask` to make task management slightly faster. 1. Create or clone a `~/.dstask` git repository for the data, if you haven't already: - Linux/macOS: `mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init` - Windows: `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.dstask && git -C %USERPROFILE%\.dstask init` ## PowerShell completion Save the completion script to a file and source it in your PowerShell profile: ```powershell dstask powershell-completion > ~\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\dstask-completion.ps1 Add-Content $PROFILE '. ~/Documents/WindowsPowerShell/dstask-completion.ps1' ``` ## Usage Run `dstask help` for usage information. ### Basic Commands - `dstask add [tags] [project:name] [priority:P0-P3]` - Add a new task - `dstask` or `dstask next` - Show next tasks to work on - `dstask start` - Start working on a task - `dstask stop` - Stop working on a task - `dstask done` - Mark a task as complete - `dstask edit` - Edit a task - `dstask note` - Edit the markdown note for a task - `dstask open` - Open URLs in task and note - `dstask show-open` - Show all open tasks - `dstask show-resolved` - Show completed tasks - `dstask show-paused` - Show paused tasks - `dstask context ` - Switch to a context (filter) - `dstask sync` - Synchronise with git remote ### Task Properties - **Priority**: P0 (highest), P1, P2 (default), P3 (lowest) - **Tags**: Add with `+tag`, remove with `-tag` - **Projects**: Set with `project:name` - **Due dates**: Set with `due:YYYY-MM-DD` - **Status**: open, active, paused, resolved ### Contexts Contexts automatically filter tasks and apply tags to new tasks: ```bash dstask context work dstask add finish report # automatically tagged with +work dstask # shows only work tasks dstask context -- # clear context ``` ### Git Sync Sync your tasks across devices using git: ```bash # Set up sync on first device cd ~/.dstask git remote add origin git push -u origin master # On other devices git clone ~/.dstask # To sync dstask sync ``` ### Templates Create task templates for recurring patterns: ```bash dstask add template +template project:meetings priority:P1 dstask add from-template ``` ## Best Practices - Create contexts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus. - Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most. - Keep task summaries brief. Use the note field for details, checklists, and context. - Use dstask to track things you might forget, rather than everything. SNR is important. Don't track tasks for the sake of it, and don't track _ideas_. Track ideas separately. - Spend regular time reviewing tasks. You'll probably find some you've already resolved, and many you've forgotten. The `show-unorganised` command is good for this. - Try to work through tasks from the top of the list. Dstask sorts by priority then creation date -- the most important tasks are at the top. - Use `start`/`stop` to mark what you're genuinely working on right now; it makes resuming work faster. Paused tasks will be slightly highlighted, so you won't lose track of them. `show-paused` helps if they start to pile up. - Keep a [github-style check list](https://help.github.com/en/articles/about-task-lists) in the markdown note of complex or procedural tasks - Failing to get started working? Start with the smallest task - Record only required tasks. Track ideas separately, else your task list will grow unboundedly! - set `DSTASK_CONTEXT` in a `.envrc` per-project repository. With direnv, this allows you to automatically switch context ## Database The default database location is: - Linux/macOS: `~/.dstask/` - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dstask` It can be configured by the environment variable `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`. ## Integration of fuzzy finders Instead of passing task IDs to commands, a fuzzy finder like [*fzf*](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) can be used to search tasks by their summary instead. This is not part of dstask itself, but can be achieved by defining a shell wrapper like this in your `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`: ```bash function dstask () { local has_double_dash subcommand if (( $# == 1 || $# == 2 )); then has_double_dash="$( [[ "$1" == "--" || "$2" == "--" ]] && echo "1" || echo "0" )" subcommand="$( [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && echo "$2" || echo "$1" )" if (( $# == 1 || has_double_dash )) && \ [[ "${subcommand}" =~ ^(done|edit|note|open|remove|start|stop)$ ]] then command dstask show-open $( (( has_double_dash )) && echo "--" ) \ | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .summary] | @tsv' \ | fzf --delimiter='\t' --nth=2 --accept-nth=1 --preview='DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1 dstask {1} --' \ | xargs -n1 dstask "${subcommand}" return fi fi command dstask "$@" } ``` The wrapper function checks if dstask was called with a subcommand missing the task ID, and if so uses the `show-open` command to get a list of tasks to choose from. `--` can be used to ignore the current context for the fuzzy search. All other commands are passed directly to dstask. ## Alternatives Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal. - [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell - [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue - [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support - [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli) - [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager - [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy ## FAQ > Does dstask encrypt tasks? Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote repository encrypted, you may consider [git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or [git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the tools themselves. > Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter? Yes. 1. Set a context: 2. Run a modify command without and ID 3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers. You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command. > Is there a GUI or web interface? Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go via a smartphone: . It's in early stages but is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people. > Has dstask been featured in a magazine? Yes! :-) [releases]: https://github.com/naggie/dstask/releases

# wire bash completions to dstask completion engine. Some of the workarounds for
# idiosyncrasies around separation with colons taken from /etc/bash_completion

_dstask() {
    # reconstruct COMP_WORDS to re-join separations caused by colon (which is a default separator)
    # yes, this method ends up splitting by spaces, but that's not a problem for the dstask parser
    # see http://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/FAQ
    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    # hand to dstask as canonical args
    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

complete -F _dstask dstask
complete -F _dstask task
#complete -F _dstask n
#complete -F _dstask t

function.arguments:
{"command":"TEST_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
git -C $TEST_DIR init
git -C $TEST_DIR config user.email "test@example.com"
git -C $TEST_DIR config user.name "Test User"
export DSTASK_GIT_REPO=$TEST_DIR

./executable add Task P0 P0
./executable add Task P1 P1 project:myproj +web
./executable add Task P2 / note on P2
./executable 1 start
./executable 3 stop

echo "--- NON-TTY OUTPUT FOR DSTASK ---"
./executable

echo "--- TTY OUTPUT FOR DSTASK (using python pty) ---"
python3 -c "
import pty, os
master, slave = pty.openpty()
pid = os.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.close(master)
    os.dup2(slave, 0)
    os.dup2(slave, 1)
    os.dup2(slave, 2)
    os.execv('./executable', ['./executable'])
else:
    os.close(slave)
    output = os.read(master, 10240)
    print(output.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
"

rm -rf $TEST_DIR"}
function.name: bash

import pty, os, fcntl, termios, struct
master, slave = pty.openpty()
fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 24, 100, 0, 0))
if os.fork() == 0:
    os.close(master); os.dup2(slave, 0); os.dup2(slave, 1); os.dup2(slave, 2)
    os.execv('./executable', ['./executable', 'show-open'])
else:

    output = b''
    while True:
        try:
            c = os.read(master, 1024)
            if not c: break
            output += c
        except OSError: break
    print(repr(output.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')))
"

rm -rf $TEST_DIR"}

            output += c

# wire bash completions to dstask completion engine. Some of the workarounds for
# idiosyncrasies around separation with colons taken from /etc/bash_completion

_dstask() {
    # reconstruct COMP_WORDS to re-join separations caused by colon (which is a default separator)
    # yes, this method ends up splitting by spaces, but that's not a problem for the dstask parser
    # see http://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/FAQ
    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    # hand to dstask as canonical args
    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

complete -F _dstask dstask
complete -F _dstask task

#complete -F _dstask t

#autoload

    compadd -- $(dstask _completions "${words[@]}")
}

specified with + (or - for filtering) eg: +work. The project is specified with

#!/bin/sh
sed -i 's/status: pending/status: active/' "$1"
sed -i 's/summary: Task 1/summary: Edited Task 1/' "$1"
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/myeditor.sh

./executable add Task 1

python3 -c "
import pty, os, fcntl, termios, struct
master, slave = pty.openpty()
fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 24, 100, 0, 0))
env = dict(os.environ)
env['EDITOR'] = '/tmp/myeditor.sh'
if os.fork() == 0:
    os.close(master); os.dup2(slave, 0); os.dup2(slave, 1); os.dup2(slave, 2)
    os.execve('./executable', ['./executable', 'edit', '1'], env)
else:
    os.close(slave)
    output = b''
    while True:
        try:
            c = os.read(master, 1024)
            if not c: break
            output += c
        except OSError: break
    print(repr(output.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')))
"

echo "=== ACTIVE DIR ==="
ls -la $TEST_DIR/active/
cat $TEST_DIR/active/*.yml

git -C $TEST_DIR log --oneline

rm -rf $TEST_DIR /tmp/myeditor.sh"}

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"

const BASH_COMPLETION = `# wire bash completions to dstask completion engine. Some of the workarounds for
# idiosyncrasies around separation with colons taken from /etc/bash_completion

_dstask() {
    # reconstruct COMP_WORDS to re-join separations caused by colon (which is a default separator)
    # yes, this method ends up splitting by spaces, but that's not a problem for the dstask parser
    # see http://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/FAQ
    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    # hand to dstask as canonical args
    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

complete -F _dstask dstask
complete -F _dstask task
#complete -F _dstask n
#complete -F _dstask t
`

const ZSH_COMPLETION = `#compdef dstask
#autoload


_dstask() {
    compadd -- $(dstask _completions "${words[@]}")
}

compdef _dstask dstask
`

const FISH_COMPLETION = `#!/usr/bin/env fish

complete -f -c dstask -a (echo (dstask _completions) | string collect)
#complete -f -c task -a (echo (task _completions) | string collect)
#complete -f -c t -a (echo (t _completions) | string collect)

`

func Completions(ts *TaskSet, args []string) {
	var items []string
	baseCmds := []string{
		CMD_NEXT, CMD_ADD, "rm", CMD_REMOVE, CMD_TEMPLATE, CMD_LOG, CMD_START,
		CMD_NOTE, "notes", CMD_STOP, CMD_DONE, "resolve", CMD_CONTEXT, CMD_MODIFY,
		CMD_EDIT, CMD_UNDO, CMD_SYNC, CMD_OPEN, CMD_GIT, "show-next", CMD_SHOW_PROJECTS,
		CMD_SHOW_TAGS, CMD_SHOW_ACTIVE, CMD_SHOW_PAUSED, CMD_SHOW_OPEN, CMD_SHOW_RESOLVED,
		CMD_SHOW_TEMPLATES, CMD_SHOW_UNORGANISED, CMD_BASH_COMPLETION, CMD_FISH_COMPLETION,
		CMD_ZSH_COMPLETION, CMD_HELP, CMD_VERSION,
		PRIORITY_P0, PRIORITY_P1, PRIORITY_P2, PRIORITY_P3,
	}
	items = append(items, baseCmds...)

	projectsMap := make(map[string]bool)
	tagsMap := make(map[string]bool)

	for _, t := range ts.Tasks {
		if t.Project != "" {
			projectsMap[t.Project] = true
		}
		for _, tag := range t.Tags {
			tagsMap[tag] = true
		}
	}

	for proj := range projectsMap {
		items = append(items, "project:"+proj)
		items = append(items, "-project:"+proj)
	}

	for tag := range tagsMap {
		items = append(items, "+"+tag)
		items = append(items, "-"+tag)
	}

	prefix := ""
	if len(args) > 0 {
		prefix = args[len(args)-1]
	}

	var matched []string
	seen := make(map[string]bool)
	for _, item := range items {
		if !seen[item] && strings.HasPrefix(item, prefix) {
			seen[item] = true
			matched = append(matched, item)
		}
	}

	for _, item := range matched {
		fmt.Println(item)
	}
}

def run_workflow(binary):
    dir_repo = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'init'], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com'], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'config', 'user.name', 'Test User'], capture_output=True)

    env = dict(os.environ, DSTASK_GIT_REPO=dir_repo)

    outputs = []
    cmds = [
        ['add', 'Task 1', '+work', 'P1', 'project:proj1'],
        ['add', 'Task 2', '+home', 'P0', 'due:2026-12-31'],
        ['add', 'Task 3', '+work', 'P2'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['1', 'start'],
        ['show-active'],
        ['1', 'stop'],
        ['show-paused'],
        ['context', '+work'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['2', 'done', 'closed note'],
        ['show-resolved'],
        ['show-projects'],
        ['show-tags'],
        ['context', 'none'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['1', 'remove'],
        ['show-open'],
    ]

    for c in cmds:
        r = subprocess.run([binary] + c, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        outputs.append((c, r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr))

    shutil.rmtree(dir_repo)
    return outputs

out_orig = run_workflow('./executable')
out_new = run_workflow('./build_test')

diffs = 0
for (c_o, ret_o, st_o, err_o), (c_n, ret_n, st_n, err_n) in zip(out_orig, out_new):
    clean_o = re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', 'UUID', st_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', 'UUID', st_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'\[master [^\]]+\]', '[master HASH]', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'\[master [^\]]+\]', '[master HASH]', clean_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'created\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'created\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'created\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'created\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'resolved\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'resolved\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'resolved\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'resolved\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_n)

    if ret_o != ret_n or clean_o != clean_n or err_o != err_n:
        diffs += 1
        print(f'DIFF in cmd: {c_o}')
        if ret_o != ret_n: print(f'  Returncodes: orig {ret_o} vs new {ret_n}')
        if clean_o != clean_n: print(f'  Stdout orig:\n{repr(clean_o)}\n  Stdout new:\n{repr(clean_n)}')
        if err_o != err_n: print(f'  Stderr orig:\n{repr(err_o)}\n  Stderr new:\n{repr(err_n)}')

if diffs == 0:

import subprocess, os, shutil, tempfile, json, re

def run_workflow(binary):
    dir_repo = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'init'], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com'], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'config', 'user.name', 'Test User'], capture_output=True)

    env = dict(os.environ, DSTASK_GIT_REPO=dir_repo)

    outputs = []
    cmds = [
        ['add', 'Task 1', '+work', 'P1', 'project:proj1'],
        ['add', 'Task 2', '+home', 'P0', 'due:2026-12-31'],
        ['add', 'Task 3', '+work', 'P2'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['1', 'start'],
        ['show-active'],
        ['1', 'stop'],
        ['show-paused'],
        ['context', '+work'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['2', 'done', 'closed note'],
        ['show-resolved'],
        ['show-projects'],
        ['show-tags'],
        ['context', 'none'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['1', 'remove'],
        ['show-open'],
    ]

    for c in cmds:
        r = subprocess.run([binary] + c, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        outputs.append((c, r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr))

    shutil.rmtree(dir_repo)
    return outputs

out_orig = run_workflow('./executable')
out_new = run_workflow('./build_test')

diffs = 0
for (c_o, ret_o, st_o, err_o), (c_n, ret_n, st_n, err_n) in zip(out_orig, out_new):
    clean_o = re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', 'UUID', st_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', 'UUID', st_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'\[master [^\]]+\]', '[master HASH]', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'\[master [^\]]+\]', '[master HASH]', clean_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'created\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'created\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'created\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'created\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'resolved\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'resolved\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'resolved\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'resolved\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_n)

    if ret_o != ret_n or clean_o != clean_n or err_o != err_n:
        diffs += 1
        print(f'DIFF in cmd: {c_o}')
        if ret_o != ret_n: print(f'  Returncodes: orig {ret_o} vs new {ret_n}')
        if clean_o != clean_n: print(f'  Stdout orig:\n{repr(clean_o)}\n  Stdout new:\n{repr(clean_n)}')
        if err_o != err_n: print(f'  Stderr orig:\n{repr(err_o)}\n  Stderr new:\n{repr(err_n)}')

if diffs == 0:
    print('ALL WORKFLOW COMMANDS MATCHED PERFECTLY!')
""}

def run_workflow(binary):
    dir_repo = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'init'], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com'], capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', dir_repo, 'config', 'user.name', 'Test User'], capture_output=True)

    env = dict(os.environ, DSTASK_GIT_REPO=dir_repo)

    outputs = []
    cmds = [
        ['add', 'Task 1', '+work', 'P1', 'project:proj1'],
        ['add', 'Task 2', '+home', 'P0', 'due:2026-12-31'],
        ['add', 'Task 3', '+work', 'P2'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['1', 'start'],
        ['show-active'],
        ['1', 'stop'],
        ['show-paused'],
        ['context', '+work'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['2', 'done', 'closed note'],
        ['show-resolved'],
        ['show-projects'],
        ['show-tags'],
        ['context', 'none'],
        ['show-open'],
        ['1', 'remove'],
        ['show-open'],
    ]

    for c in cmds:
        r = subprocess.run([binary] + c, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
        outputs.append((c, r.returncode, r.stdout, r.stderr))

    shutil.rmtree(dir_repo)
    return outputs

out_orig = run_workflow('./executable')
out_new = run_workflow('./build_test')

diffs = 0
for (c_o, ret_o, st_o, err_o), (c_n, ret_n, st_n, err_n) in zip(out_orig, out_new):
    clean_o = re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', 'UUID', st_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', 'UUID', st_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'\[master [^\]]+\]', '[master HASH]', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'\[master [^\]]+\]', '[master HASH]', clean_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'created\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'created\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'created\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'created\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_n)
    clean_o = re.sub(r'resolved\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'resolved\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_o)
    clean_n = re.sub(r'resolved\": \"[^\"]+\"', 'resolved\": \"TIMESTAMP\"', clean_n)

    if ret_o != ret_n or clean_o != clean_n or err_o != err_n:
        diffs += 1
        print(f'DIFF in cmd: {c_o}')
        if ret_o != ret_n: print(f'  Returncodes: orig {ret_o} vs new {ret_n}')
        if clean_o != clean_n: print(f'  Stdout orig:\n{repr(clean_o)}\n  Stdout new:\n{repr(clean_n)}')
        if err_o != err_n: print(f'  Stderr orig:\n{repr(err_o)}\n  Stderr new:\n{repr(err_n)}')

if diffs == 0:
    print('ALL WORKFLOW COMMANDS MATCHED PERFECTLY!')

import pty, os, fcntl, termios, struct, subprocess, tempfile, shutil

def test_tty_cmd(cmd):
    dir_orig = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    dir_new = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    for d in (dir_orig, dir_new):
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, 'init'], capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, 'config', 'user.email', 'test@example.com'], capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, 'config', 'user.name', 'Test User'], capture_output=True)

    # Add sample tasks to both
    env_o = dict(os.environ, DSTASK_GIT_REPO=dir_orig)
    env_n = dict(os.environ, DSTASK_GIT_REPO=dir_new)

    for bin_path, env in [('./executable', env_o), ('./build_test', env_n)]:
        subprocess.run([bin_path, 'add', 'Task 1', '+work', 'P1', 'project:proj1'], env=env, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run([bin_path, 'add', 'Task 2', '+home', 'P0', 'due:2026-12-31'], env=env, capture_output=True)

    def run_pty(bin_path, env):
        master, slave = pty.openpty()
        fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 24, 100, 0, 0))
        p = subprocess.Popen([bin_path] + cmd, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, stdin=slave, env=env)
        os.close(slave)
        out = b''
        while True:
            try:
                c = os.read(master, 1024)
                if not c: break
                out += c
            except OSError: break
        os.close(master)
        p.wait()
        return out.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')

    out_o = run_pty('./executable', env_o)
    out_n = run_pty('./build_test', env_n)

    shutil.rmtree(dir_orig)
    shutil.rmtree(dir_new)

    return (out_o, out_n)

for c in [['show-open'], ['show-projects'], ['show-tags']]:
    o, n = test_tty_cmd(c)
    print(f'=== TTY CMD: {c} ===')
    if o == n:
        print('MATCH!')
    else:
        print('DIFF:')
        print('ORIG:', repr(o))
        print('NEW: ', repr(n))
""}

I have implemented the complete source code for `dstask` in Go.

### Summary of Reimplementation

1. **Core Architecture**:
   - **Task Management**: Implemented YAML serialization and deserialization for tasks, tracking properties like summary, notes, tags, project, priority, created/resolved/due timestamps, and status directories (`pending`, `active`, `paused`, `resolved`, `template`, `deferred`, `delegated`, `recurring`).
   - **ID Management**: Maintained stable ID mapping using git log history and creation timestamps.
   - **Query & Filter Engine**: Parsed CLI arguments and global context filters (`+tag`, `-tag`, `project:name`, `-project:name`, priorities `P0`-`P3`, `due:...`, `/ notes`).
   - **State Persistence**: Serialized global context filter state using Go `gob` encoding at `.git/dstask/state.bin`.
   - **Git Operations**: Handled git initialization, commits with custom messages (`Added`, `Started`, `Stopped`, `Resolved`, `Removed:`, `Modified`, `Edit note`), undo, sync (`pull`/`push`), and git pass-through.
   - **CLI & Output Rendering**: Formatted terminal output for TTY (ANSI color-coded tables with row striping, priority colors, status colors, and responsive column sizing) and JSON output for non-TTY environments.

2. **Build and Setup**:
   - Created `compile.sh` to compile the codebase into `./executable`.
   - Added `.gitignore` to exclude build artifacts.
   - Committed all source code files to the git repository.
